messages:
maria: Ran a perf trace on staging — seeing intermittent CPU spikes in the scheduler path during tokenization. Looking for quick eyes.
kevin: Which trace did you run, nsys or perf?
jyoti: +1, also share the perf script snippet if you have it.
maria: perf + FlameGraph. Here's a perf script snippet from a bad spike:
```
futex_wait+0x30
__pthread_mutex_lock+0x1a
_PyEval_EvalFrameDefault+0x4b2
Scheduler._schedule_batch+0x1f
Batcher.append+0x2d
tokenizer._fast_split+0x8a
__GI___libc_malloc+0x7b
```
jyoti: That looks like futex contention + allocator hot path. Any KV-cache warmup?
maria: KV warmed. Repro on low concurrency too. The hot path is dominated by Python scheduler lock acquisition that occasionally takes 3-4ms.
sam: Try LD_PRELOAD=jemalloc and rerun?
maria: Did that — median improved ~30% but the tail spikes still occur. Another perf stack from the tail shows:
```
futex_wait -> PyGILState_Ensure -> tokenize.c:init_singleton -> malloc -> arena_lock
```
kevin: Did you record page faults? perf record -e page-faults?
maria: Yes. Minor faults spike concurrently — looks like lazy mmap/page-in when tokenizer C-extension hits first code path.
jyoti: If the C extension lazily allocates internal buffers on first call, that could explain cold spikes. But you said low concurrency too — are we seeing repeated init?
maria: I added tracepoints for Scheduler.lock_wait_ms. Avg ~120us, but 99.9th ~3.6ms. Correlates with concurrent GC (gc.collect) runs.
sam: :eyes: Try disabling GC in an experiment (gc.disable()) or set PYTHONMALLOC=malloc to see effect.
maria: Disabling GC in test removes spikes entirely. So GC + malloc arenas + tokenizer lazy init = culprit triangle.
kevin: Can you produce a minimal repro script so I can perf locally and try pre-init?
maria: Yep — small warmup script I used:
```
# warm_tokenizer.py
import tokenizer_ext
# force early init of C extension internals
try:
    tokenizer_ext.init()
except AttributeError:
    # older builds init on import
    pass
```
Run like: `perf record -F 99 -g -- python warm_tokenizer.py && perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./flamegraph.pl > svg`

maria: TL;DR: GC interplay with allocator and C-extension lazy init causes tail latency in scheduler during batch flush. Proposed mitigations: 1) switch runtime image to jemalloc in Dedicated, 2) change tokenizer ext to eager-init on process start, 3) add GC-safe flush window in Scheduler to avoid concurrent collect during critical section.
kevin: I can try eager init patch tomorrow. Can you attach perf flame and perf-record artifacts to the ticket?
maria: Will attach. Filing a regression ticket.
perf-bot: New ticket INF-7821 created by maria: "scheduler tail spikes due to GC+malloc during tokenizer init" :ticket: 
maria: Thanks — adding perf flames to INF-7821 and assigning to @kevin and @jyoti if they pick it up.
